newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Victorias says to pay interest payment.
newsitem.headline: Victorias says to pay interest payment.

text.p: Cash-strapped Victorias Milling Corp has enough funds to meet monthly interest payments due this afternoon on its 4.423 billion pesos debt, an official of the sugar miller said on Friday.
"The check is ready for deposit. We have enough funds to update payments on all our 32 creditors," the official, who requested not to be named, told Reuters in a phone interview.
The company official declined to disclose the amount of the interest payments.
On Thursday, the Philippine's largest sugar miller said its creditors agreed to peg its peso-denominated loans based on the 90-day Treasury bill rate plus a spread of three percentage points.
It also said its creditors agreed to peg its foreign loans based ont the LIBOR rate plus a spread of three percentage points.
The firm said the loan pricing was done at a March 11 meeting with its creditors.The company did not disclose the previous pricing of the loans.
Victorias has obtained a 90-day reprive on principal payments on its debt.
About 10 to 12 banks of the total 32 creditors have collaterals on their loans. Seven foreign banks are also included in the creditor group.
